package_info.package_manager: npm (coa, rc, ua-parser-js); standalone binary (PuTTY, RealVNC)
package_info.package_versions: coa@2.0.3, rc@1.2.9, ua-parser-js@0.7.29, ua-parser-js@0.7.30 (hijacked npm versions); specific weaponized builds of PuTTY and RealVNC (no official version numbers, but trojanized installers/binaries as described in the report)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages and applications were compromised by threat actors who injected malicious code into trusted open source projects and widely used remote access tools. The modifications enabled the execution of unauthorized code on victim systems, including credential theft, data exfiltration, and installation of persistent backdoors. Attackers exploited the trust and distribution reach of these tools to maximize the impact of their supply chain attacks.

required_permissions: filesystem (write to disk, create autorun entries)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious loader code embedded in the trojanized PuTTY/RealVNC binary. The report describes this as code that 'loads the system with services that can be used to load further malware', establishing persistence and enabling remote attacker control. (Actual binary code not shown in the report.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Installs unauthorized Windows services or background processes to maintain persistence and facilitate the download or execution of additional attacker-controlled payloads. May also modify system autorun entries or registry keys to ensure continued execution after reboot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate versions of PuTTY and RealVNC do not install hidden services or background loaders unrelated to their documented remote access functionality. The presence of new, undocumented services or autorun entries created by these binaries is a strong indicator of compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: PuTTY and RealVNC provide terminal/remote access without installing persistent background services or modifying system startup. Malicious behavior: Installs hidden services or autorun mechanisms to maintain attacker access and enable further payload delivery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment tools may install services for management purposes, but these are documented, require user/admin consent, and are signed by the vendor.
key_indicators: Creation of new Windows services or autorun registry entries by PuTTY.exe or RealVNC.exe
Persistence mechanisms (e.g., scheduled tasks, registry Run keys) not present in official releases
No user notification or consent for service installation
Modified binary hash differing from official vendor release

execution_context.trigger: import-time or postinstall (npm package installation or first use)
execution_context.file_location: index.js or postinstall script in package.json (e.g., coa@2.0.3, rc@1.2.9, ua-parser-js@0.7.29-0.7.30)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript code injected into the entry point (index.js) or postinstall script of hijacked npm packages. The code reads environment variables and credential files, then exfiltrates this data to a remote attacker-controlled server via HTTP requests. (Actual code not shown in the report, but described as 'exfiltrates environment variables and credentials to a remote server'.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Harvests sensitive data such as environment variables, authentication tokens, and credentials from the victim's system, then transmits this information to attacker infrastructure during package installation or import.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate npm packages should not access or transmit environment variables or credentials to external servers, especially via obfuscated code in entry points or install scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: Packages perform only their documented functionality and do not access or exfiltrate sensitive data. Malicious behavior: Reads secrets and sends them to untrusted remote endpoints without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may collect anonymized telemetry or crash reports, but this is always documented, opt-in, and does not include sensitive credentials.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or minified code in index.js or postinstall scripts
Network requests to hardcoded, untrusted, or non-canonical domains during install/import
Access to process.env or reading of credential/config files
No documentation or user consent for data collection

attack_chain.action: Victim is tricked into downloading and executing a trojanized open source tool (PuTTY/RealVNC) or installing a hijacked npm package (coa, rc, ua-parser-js) via social engineering, phishing, or supply chain compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial code execution on the victim's machine

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes: trojanized binaries install unauthorized loader services for persistence (snippet_1); hijacked npm packages exfiltrate environment variables and credentials (snippet_2).
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence on the system and/or exfiltration of sensitive data

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages established persistence or stolen credentials to deploy additional malware, move laterally within the network, or escalate privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, lateral movement, or further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected creation of Windows services or autorun entries by PuTTY.exe or RealVNC.exe
Obfuscated or minified JavaScript in npm package entry points (index.js) or postinstall scripts
Outbound network requests to untrusted or non-canonical domains during npm package install/import
Access to process.env or credential files by packages not requiring such access
file_indicators: Modified binaries of PuTTY.exe or RealVNC.exe with hashes differing from official releases
Presence of obfuscated JavaScript in index.js or postinstall scripts of coa, rc, or ua-parser-js
Unexpected new Windows services or autorun registry entries created after running PuTTY/RealVNC
npm package versions known to be hijacked (coa@2.0.3, rc@1.2.9, ua-parser-js@0.7.29, ua-parser-js@0.7.30)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs as listed in the report (if specific IOCs are provided, include them here)
Exfiltration of environment variables or credential data during npm install/import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for creation of unauthorized Windows services or autorun entries by PuTTY.exe or RealVNC.exe. Use file integrity monitoring to detect modified binaries with non-matching hashes. Scan npm package entry points and postinstall scripts for obfuscated or minified code, especially in known hijacked versions. Alert on outbound network connections to untrusted domains during or immediately after package installation. Employ automated supply chain security tools to flag known malicious package versions and unauthorized code changes.
